name: fitness-applied/wod-benchmarks
note: One or two lines of background for the named workouts, in Chris's voice, keyed by the workout's name (case and punctuation ignored). Written from general knowledge of the CrossFit benchmarks; every Hero line names a real person, so Chris checks each one against CrossFit.com's Hero and Girl pages before launch and removes any he cannot confirm. Names not listed get no background, only the generated introduction.

fran.background: The one everybody knows. Thrusters and pull-ups, 21-15-9, first posted on CrossFit.com in 2003. Short, and it feels like the last 400 meters of a race the whole way through.

helen.background: One of the original CrossFit "Girls". Three rounds of a run, kettlebell swings and pull-ups. It rewards a steady run more than a fast one.

diane.background: An original Girl: heavy deadlifts and handstand push-ups, 21-15-9. The deadlift weight is the test. If it isn't there yet, scale it and keep the rep scheme.

elizabeth.background: An original Girl: squat cleans and ring dips, 21-15-9. The cleans are the work; the dips are where the shoulders quit.

grace.background: Thirty clean and jerks for time. One of the original Girls, and one of the few you can finish in under two minutes if the bar is right.

isabel.background: Thirty snatches for time. Grace's sister. Same idea, harder lift.

jackie.background: A 1,000-meter row, 50 light thrusters, 30 pull-ups. The row sets up everything after it. Row steady, not angry.

karen.background: 150 wall-ball shots for time. That's it. That's the whole workout, and it's enough.

linda.background: The "three bars of death": deadlift, bench press and clean, 10 down to 1, with the weights set by your bodyweight. You need three bars loaded before you start.

mary.background: A 20-minute AMRAP of handstand push-ups, pistols and pull-ups. Cindy's harder sister.

nancy.background: Five rounds: a 400-meter run and 15 overhead squats. The run makes the squats shaky. That's the point.

angie.background: 100 pull-ups, 100 push-ups, 100 sit-ups, 100 squats, each finished before the next one starts. A test of how well you break things up.

annie.background: Double-unders and sit-ups, 50-40-30-20-10. If your double-unders are good, it's fast. If they aren't, it teaches you patience.

barbara.background: Five rounds of pull-ups, push-ups, sit-ups and squats, with three minutes of rest between rounds. Each round is scored on its own.

chelsea.background: Every minute on the minute for 30 minutes: 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, 15 squats. Miss a minute and you're done. Cindy with a clock on it.

cindy.background: A 20-minute AMRAP of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, 15 squats. The best test of steady pacing in the gym. Twenty rounds is a very good score.

eva.background: Five rounds: 800-meter run, 30 heavy kettlebell swings, 30 pull-ups. A long one. Most people take 40 minutes or more.

kelly.background: Five rounds: 400-meter run, 30 box jumps, 30 wall-ball shots. Legs the whole way.

lynne.background: Five rounds of max-rep bodyweight bench press and max-rep pull-ups, resting as needed. Scored by total reps, not time.

nicole.background: A 20-minute AMRAP of a 400-meter run and max-rep pull-ups. Your score is the total pull-ups. The run is your rest.

amanda.background: Muscle-ups and squat snatches, 9-7-5. Short, technical, and honest about your skill.

christine.background: Three rounds: 500-meter row, 12 bodyweight deadlifts, 21 box jumps. Simple and fast if you keep moving.

fight gone bad.background: Built for a fighter: five stations, one minute each, one minute off, three rounds, 17 minutes total. Score every rep. The name came from the fighter's own answer when asked how it compared to a bout.

filthy 50.background: Ten movements, 50 reps each, in order. A long chipper. Pick a pace you can keep for all ten.

nasty girls.background: Three rounds: 50 squats, 7 muscle-ups, 10 hang power cleans. The muscle-ups decide it.

the chief.background: Five three-minute AMRAPs of 3 power cleans, 6 push-ups, 9 squats, with a minute of rest between each. Start each round where you left off.

hope.background: Fight Gone Bad's format with different stations, first run as a fundraiser workout. Three rounds, a minute at each, score total reps.

murph.background: For Navy Lt. Michael Murphy, killed in Afghanistan on June 28, 2005. He called this workout "Body Armor". A mile run, 100 pull-ups, 200 push-ups, 300 squats, a mile run, in a 20-lb vest if you have one. Partition the middle any way you like.

dt.background: For Air Force Staff Sgt. Timothy P. Davis, killed in Afghanistan on February 20, 2009. Five rounds of deadlifts, hang power cleans and push jerks at one weight. Grip is what fails first.

j t.background: For Navy Petty Officer 1st Class Jeff Taylor, killed in Afghanistan on June 28, 2005. Handstand push-ups, ring dips and push-ups, 21-15-9. All pushing, all shoulders.

michael.background: For Navy Lt. Michael McGreevy Jr., killed in Afghanistan on June 28, 2005. Three rounds: an 800-meter run, 50 back extensions, 50 sit-ups.

daniel.background: For Army Sgt. 1st Class Daniel Crabtree, killed in Iraq on June 8, 2006. Pull-ups, runs and thrusters, bookended by 50 pull-ups each side.

randy.background: For LAPD SWAT Officer Randy Simmons, killed in the line of duty on February 7, 2008. Seventy-five power snatches at a light weight, for time.

nate.background: For Navy Chief Petty Officer Nate Hardy, killed in Iraq on February 4, 2008. A 20-minute AMRAP of muscle-ups, handstand push-ups and heavy kettlebell swings.

manion.background: For Marine 1st Lt. Travis Manion, killed in Iraq on April 29, 2007. Seven rounds of a 400-meter run and 29 back squats.

tommy v.background: For Navy Senior Chief Petty Officer Thomas Valentine, who died in a training accident on February 13, 2008. Thrusters and rope climbs, 21-15-9 and 12-9-6.

holleyman.background: For Army Sgt. 1st Class Aaron Holleyman, killed in Iraq on August 30, 2004. Thirty rounds of 5 wall-ball shots, 3 handstand push-ups, 1 power clean.

loredo.background: For Army Staff Sgt. Edwardo Loredo, killed in Afghanistan on June 24, 2010. Six rounds of squats, push-ups, walking lunges and a run.

abbate.background: For Marine Sgt. Matthew Abbate, killed in Afghanistan on December 2, 2010. A long one: runs and heavy clean and jerks.

bradley.background: For Air Force Senior Airman Bradley Smith, killed in Afghanistan on January 3, 2010. Ten rounds of sprints, pull-ups and burpees with rest built in.

jerry.background: For Army Sgt. Maj. Jerry Dwayne Patton, who died in Afghanistan on October 15, 2008. A mile run, a 2,000-meter row, a mile run. All engine.

luce.background: For Army Capt. Ronald G. Luce, killed in Afghanistan on August 2, 2009. Three rounds of a run, muscle-ups and squats, in a vest.

clovis.background: For Army 2nd Lt. Clovis T. Ray, killed in Afghanistan on March 15, 2012. A 10-mile run with 150 burpee pull-ups, split however you want.

jack.background: For Army Staff Sgt. Jack M. Martin III, killed in the Philippines on September 29, 2009. A 20-minute AMRAP of push presses, kettlebell swings and box jumps.

joshie.background: For Army Staff Sgt. Joshua Whitaker, killed in Afghanistan on May 15, 2007. Three rounds of dumbbell snatches and L pull-ups.

emily.background: For Army 2nd Lt. Emily Perez, killed in Iraq on September 12, 2006. Ten rounds of double-unders, pull-ups, push-ups and a run.

riley.background: For Army Sgt. 1st Class Riley Stephens, killed in Afghanistan on September 28, 2012. A mile run, 150 burpees, a mile run, in a vest.

chad1000x.background: For Navy SEAL Chad Wilkinson, lost in 2018. One thousand box step-ups with a weighted pack. His family built it so people would move together and talk.

chad.background: For Navy SEAL Chad Wilkinson, lost in 2018. One thousand box step-ups with a weighted pack. His family built it so people would move together and talk.

operation red wings.background: For the 19 service members killed in Operation Red Wings in Afghanistan on June 28, 2005, Lt. Michael Murphy among them.
